newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM says still actively seeking Europartner.
newsitem.headline: KLM says still actively seeking Europartner.

text.p: Dutch carrier KLM said on Wednesday it was keeping all its options open in its search for a European partner and denied it had missed its opportunity to forge a major Euro-alliance.
"The necessity (of finding a partner) depends on the speed of consolidation in the European market...KLM is still in a very good position," KLM president Pieter Bouw told a results news conference.
He said the process of consolidation within the European market had been considerably delayed, with many airlines taking time out to restructure.
"Until that process is rounded off, we will continue to keep our options open," Bouw said, adding that the European market still remained very fragmented.
"The cards have not all yet been dealt in the international alliance game," he said. "KLM maintains its goal of becoming a major European player in a leading Global Airline System."
While KLM's existing European alliances with airlines such as Air UK and Eurowings were small, they were solid, he said.
"Together with our regional partners we are developing a regional brand with an accompanying service concept," he said.
Within six months KLM would unveil a far more high-profile product for its European activities, Bouw said.
